newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank says higher primary surplus needed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank says higher primary surplus needed.

text.p: The monetary policy director of Brazil's Central Bank Francisco Lopes said Tuesday Brazil must increase its primary surplus in order to prevent a sharp increase in net public sector debt.
But Lopes, talking to reporters at an international seminar on public finance, said suggestions the primary surplus should represent 3-4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) were exaggerated.
Lopes said that in order to halt debt growth, a primary surplus of about 1.5 percent of GDP was needed.
Analysts speaking earlier at the seminar said they expected Brazil to report a primary surplus of about one percent in 1996.
"We still need to improve our primary surplus, but to say that a primary surplus of 3-4 percent is needed to stop an explosion of debt is exaggerated," the official said.

Lopes said evaluations of Brazil's debt situation should consider one-off "distortions", like Banco do Brasil's 7.8 billion real first half loss and plans to securitize a roughly 50 billion real shortfall in the federal FCVS housing fund.
Lopes estimated that the real interest rate cost of Brazil's total debt was about nine percent a year.

On Monday, IMF director Vito Tanzi and the Inter-American Development Bank's chief economist Ricardo Hausmann both warned that Brazil faces growing debt problems if it fails to produce primary surpluses higher than the one percent seen for 1996.
